title: Doing it wrong
author: arkaine_23
selftext:
Amateur hour.  I lack knowledge in all relevant areas but I'm still working toward a degree of trading automation.  So given my limits here's the concept I'm working on.  I'm pretty sure that if I get this working, it will self destruct my account in short order.  Anyway....  I have skills with things like powershell and bash, and wouldn't have trouble setting up.virtual hosts or running my own servers.   When coding outside what I know, I partner with AI's to muddle through​.  I don't know python.  I have no significant trading skills either, just vibes.



The outlune of my bot is:



An AI signal app's alerts > 



AHK script on a PC > 



injest some internet data > 



evaluate conditions for go/no-go/risk level >



activate a webull hotkey to buy & TP/SL.  



If I'm around and monitoring, I'll manage adjustments after that initial order.  If not, pray the strategy is sound.  The goal is to quickly get aboard intraday big movers and exit with a conservative amount of profit or cut losses and bail on them if they fail or I'm late entering.

  
1)  Function for getting alerts   

I'll use someone else's signal/scanner AI.  I've been playing with an app called Pro Ticker Signals.   It sends iOS/Android notifications (subject to some delay), or if you have the app open you can​ refresh it's scan page for potentially faster access to its real time alerts.   These seem to mostly come premarket or around market open.   I've only been watching it for a short time, but it's been finding a handful of big intraday movers every day.   

The trick is moving fast enough. I'm mostly late in arriving because I'm asleep or working when those alerts come in and I wind up just gambling on the volatility after they've peaked and try to make a few of bucks/day from my tiny for-fun webull account.  I want to get entry automatically and build in a conservative bit of profiting on a rise and exiting on a fall as a baseline play, and see how it does.  Then I can figure out other things to try to safeguard it and optimizie it further.   



I'll need to keep an app open and refreshing and then from what it displays read text.and parse it for the data I want.  I'll use regular expressions to collect ticker names and entry/Long prices from the signal texts (ignoring short signals for now).  



2)  Function to collect other info about a ticker.

I'll also scrape yahoo http to get an alerted ticker's current (or at least its ballpark price).   I want to ignore tickers that have a current price or signaled entry price less than $1, and also ignore them if the current price is already more than 20% higher than the signal's entry price.   If the price is below the signal's.entry, then I'll loop a price re-check until current price is greater than or equal to entry price.   This loop would have a sleep period of let's say 3s per price re-evaluation, and a max limit of 300 cycles before deciding to ignore the ticker.  

  
3)  if price loop conditions were met, bring webull desktop into focus and execute one of several preset buy order hotkeys.   I'll wrap some logic around choosing which buy preset and exiting strategy to use.  I may try to read my account's settled cash so I can dynamically use a small % of that per trade, or just hardcode a max $ value per buy in the script.

  
Set a max of X tickers to execute buy orders for per day. 



At midnight, reset:  clear ingored and activated tickers and the buy count daily.  Injest or request a new available per-trade $ limit for the next day.  Cycle to a new log file, clean up any temp data/files.

comments.author: arkaine_23
comments.body:
Build log:

I have some code for the larger script's logic where my capture of the ticker/entry price is assumed to be done by mirroring the app notifications into windows- what I thought might be an easier but slower approach than screenshotting and using tesseract ocr initially.  For now that's a dummy placeholder function.   The regular expression parsing, grabbing of live price from yahoo finance, price condition evals, and sending ticker and hotkey to webull desktop are all there and ready for testing.  I need to customize some paper trade hotkeys and set these later fucntions up for a test while I work out capturing the signals.

I've split off a 2nd script for testing the signal capture from ldplayer/pro ticker signals, taking screenshots, and converting to text with tessseract ocr.  It looks like capturing the signals will run as its own process(es), and my main script will be on standby checking for the out-putted ticker/entry pairs.  I'll probably improve this later to generate order payload jsons when I figure out a better ordering platform/method.  


AHK's been finnicky about operating in the LDPlayer window.  Seems to require focusing the app and moving the cursor to it in order to do a mouse wheel up to refresh Pro Ticker Signals (the app window rejecting non-hardware mouse actions).  None of this is positionally-dependent thankfully, but it would be nice if it didn't have to bring the ldplayer window into focus.  Seems to be a common thing for the way emulators display.   The refresh action in the app creates an animation and some sleep period adjustment was needed or an error was thrown by the next action.  The next action is to mouse wheel down some so the whole watchlist is on the screen (not just the top of it), then sleep some more.   

This mouse wheel action could also be done from an LDPlayer macro and that addresses concerns about the app needing to be put in focus constantly, but taking the screenshot can't be macro'ed that way, so there'd be a timing problem doing the refresh/scrolling in ldplayer macro while using anything external to take the screenshots.  I'd wind up with partial views of the watchlist when screenshots happen while its scrolled up or refreshing.  Error handling on text collection could discard those, but I'd like to prevent them from happening in the first place and not waste time when a new signal could have come in. 

I left off at the point of AHK getting a screenshot for tesseract, but something in my syntax is failing.   I may need to adjust the method (GDI+) because its probably not finding the hwnd.  Goal:  screenshot only the ldplayer window and output to file, overwriting existing screenshot.  Not requiring focus on ldplayer window would be ideal, so nothing can interfere with the screenshot.

After that I need it to mouse wheel back up to the starting position and wait, and then repeat the loop.  Once I get the full loop operating, I'll explore methods to take the notification text from android and deliver it to the same output my screenshot/tesseract loop uses.  They can operate simultaneously and whichever is faster wins.

comments.author: arkaine_23
comments.body: So looking around at platforms, it seems like IBKR TWS may suit my needs better as far as configuring at least a trailing stop child order to a single buy hotkey, and maybe even setting a profit target that triggers trailing behavior.   I'll have to install it and explore.

comments.body: Built the kill switch.  Tailscale and Unified Remote to activate it from my phone and kill the ahk process on the computer at home.  I may also move local files the script is using and kill LDplayer or even reboot to be thorough.   Writing the script for kill, and I should be able to make one that turns everything related to the bot on in sequence with sufficient delays too.
